title: Archimedean first-slab positivity for shifted zeta canonical systems: an off-center Weil generator and a radial energy identity
description:
For ω > 0, Suzuki's shifted scattering function Θω(z) = ξ(1/2 − ω − iz)/ξ(1/2 + ω − iz) admits a prime–gamma Hankel kernel. On the prime-free first slab (depth L ≤ log 2) the arithmetic Hankel operator reduces exactly to a reflected finite-horizon Volterra convolution with completed-gamma transfer. Differentiating the transfer in the shift produces an off-center prime-free Weil form Qω,L = Q0,L + Cω,L with an explicit compact kernel. An Arb-certified Legendre calculation (512 parity–shift boxes, 16 modes per sector), closed by analytic tail bounds and independently reimplemented, proves Qω,L ≽ 6.1159·10−4 on the logarithmic form domain for 0 ≤ ω ≤ 1/2. A shift-energy identity I − V*V = 2∫0ω Vs* Qs Vs ds converts this into strict contractivity and reflection positivity I ± Hω,L ≻ 0 throughout the first slab for 0 < ω ≤ 1/2, complementing Suzuki's unconditional result for ω > 1/2. The result is prime-free and finite-depth: it proves neither the Riemann hypothesis nor a new zero-free region.

This manuscript reports computer-assisted mathematics and was prepared with substantial language-model assistance. Its verification status is recorded in Section 13 of the paper and in VERIFICATION_STATUS.md.
